note: A tune that dips under Do and comes home, learned in named stages at 40 bpm, then the low Do, Fa and Sol sung over I IV V I at 40 bpm and a line of the singer's own. The chords are tokens counted the long way (the old text named F, B♭ and C), the old Key choice is moves (key any, tempo 40 to 60), the line about another key opens with {{?key}}, and the made-up line carries the one care line.

exercise.title: A tune under Do, then over three chords
exercise.why: Tunes often dip below Do and come home, so singing under it makes Do feel like home from both sides.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then press Play again and sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Practice until the notes under {{1}} feel as sure as {{1}}.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, and the tune still dips two steps under {{1}} and comes home.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}, and {{chord:V}} the 5th, built on {{5}}.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. Sing the low {{1}} over {{chord:I}}, the low {{4}} when {{chord:IV}} comes round and {{5}} over {{chord:V}}. Sing it on "oo".
Then add {{3}} over {{chord:I}} and make up your own line.
_Don't reach for high notes: the low notes on the staff are enough for a line._
If you lose your place, hold {{1}} until {{chord:I}} comes round again.
